1.why: All seven screenshots show a static, card-based layout with no animations, carousels, or pop-up dialogs — only text, inputs and buttons.

2.why: Each step has a bold heading, a highlighted green status banner, and a single solid blue primary button, so the key action stands out, though the run-together step list and the visually prominent 'Logs' block slightly dilute the hierarchy.

3.why: Each screen contains only one task with one or two fields and one button, so the needed control is easy to locate, but the cramped/overlapping 'Your steps' text and technical Logs panel add unnecessary scanning effort.

4.why: Progress is externally shown and each screen states the next action, but the user must carry over a 64-character recovery token, a six-digit safety code and a newly created password across steps by copying them from the Logs panel.

5.why: No password manager hint, autofill attributes, 'show password', or 'remember me' option is visible anywhere — not even on the sign-in screen in step 5.

6.why: Nothing familiar or previously saved is surfaced (no masked email, no saved account, no remembered device); only completed steps turn green, which is progress rather than recognition of saved items.

7.why: Instructional sentences are short, plain and consistent ('Use your new password to securely sign in.'), although the 64-character token instruction and raw log entries are dense/technical.

8.why: No error state is shown in any of the seven screenshots — only success banners — so the claim that error messages describe problem and fix cannot be observed as true of this system.

9.why: Step 3 gives password composition rules and steps 2/4 state the expected length (64-character token, six-digit code), but no actual example input or worked demonstration is displayed anywhere.

10.why: Only a single password-based path exists; there is no visible choice among password, code or biometric login, so 'choices are clear' does not hold as there are no alternatives offered.

11.why: Each screen presents exactly one decision and at most two fields with a single primary button, so the user is never faced with many simultaneous choices.

12.why: Every step opens with an explicit green status message about the previous action ('Code confirmed…', 'Your password has been changed…', 'Privacy conditions accepted…'), plus a Logs trail and a final 'All set' confirmation.

13.why: A persistent yellow-accented 'Need help?' card appears on every screen with pause/return and anti-phishing guidance, and each step carries a one-line instruction, though there are no contextual tips for the trickier token entry.

14.why: The help card states the user can pause, refresh and return with progress saved, implying retries are possible, but no 'Back', 'Resend code', 'Start over' or edit control is visible on any screen.

15.why: All seven screens reuse the identical header, step tracker, single-card layout, green status banner, help card and Logs panel with the same typography and blue button styling.
